Drones:dji-air-3.explanation: The Air 3 records 4K/100 at up to 150 Mbps from both cameras. A U3/V30 card covers it, and a 256GB card holds close to 4 hours at the top bitrate.

Drones:dji-mini-4k.explanation: The Mini 4K records 4K/30 at up to 100 Mbps, about 12.5 MB/s, well inside a V30 card's 30 MB/s floor. DJI caps the slot at 256GB, and a 128GB card holds about 2.8 hours of 4K.

Drones:dji-mini-3.explanation: The Mini 3 records 4K/30 HDR at up to 100 Mbps, about 12.5 MB/s. DJI requires a U3/V30 card, and a 128GB card holds about 2.8 hours of 4K.

Drones:dji-mini-2-se.explanation: The Mini 2 SE records 2.7K/30 at 40 Mbps, so any U3/V30 card has plenty of margin. DJI caps the slot at 256GB, and 64GB holds over 3 hours of 2.7K.

Drones:autel-evo-ii-pro-v3.explanation: The EVO II Pro V3 records 6K/30 from a 1-inch sensor at up to 120 Mbps. Autel specifies U3/V30 microSD cards up to 256GB.

Drones:autel-evo-nano-plus.explanation: The EVO Nano+ records 4K/30 HDR to microSD. Autel requires U3/V30 cards up to 256GB, and slower cards trigger the 'Low SD card speed' warning.

Drones:autel-evo-lite-plus.explanation: The EVO Lite+ records 6K/30 and 4K/60 from a 1-inch sensor. Autel requires U3/V30 microSD cards and caps the slot at 256GB.

Drones:potensic-atom.explanation: Potensic requires a U3/V30 microSD card for the Atom, up to 256GB. Slower U1 cards are the most common cause of clips that stop after a few seconds.

Drones:potensic-atom-se.explanation: The Atom SE takes the same U3/V30 microSD cards as the standard Atom, up to 256GB. Cards below V30 cause 'write speed slow' errors and corrupted clips.

Drones:skydio-2-plus.explanation: The Skydio 2+ records 4K/60 to microSD and needs a U3/V30 card formatted exFAT. Skydio ended consumer drone sales in 2023, so buy cards that meet spec rather than hunting for official accessories.

Drones:skydio-x10.explanation: The Skydio X10 is an enterprise drone that records visual and thermal data. Use high-endurance or V60 microSD cards from a known brand and follow your fleet's data-handling policy.

Drones:fimi-mini-3.explanation: The FIMI Mini 3 records 4K/60 at up to 100 Mbps, about 12.5 MB/s. A U3/V30 card keeps up; slower cards drop frames or split the video into short clips.

Drones:holy-stone-hs175d.explanation: The HS175D only reads microSD cards up to 64GB formatted FAT32. A 32GB or 64GB Class 10 card covers its 2.7K video.

Drones:holy-stone-hs720.explanation: The HS720E and HS720G read microSD cards up to 128GB; the original HS720 may only read 32GB. The gimbal-equipped HS720G benefits from a U3/V30 card.

Drones:holy-stone-hs360s.explanation: The HS360S records 4K and needs a U3/V30 microSD card. Holy Stone lists 128GB as the maximum.

Drones:hoverair-x1-pro.explanation: The X1 Pro records up to 4K/60 and has 64GB of internal storage plus a microSD slot. HoverAir requires V30 cards between 64GB and 1TB, formatted exFAT.

Drones:hoverair-x1-pro-max.explanation: HoverAir sets V30 as the minimum for the X1 ProMax and recommends V60 for 8K/30 and 4K/120. The slot accepts 64GB to 1TB cards formatted exFAT, on top of 64GB of internal storage.

Drones:walksnail-moonlight.explanation: The Walksnail Moonlight records 4K/60 onboard and needs a U3/V30 microSD card. Walksnail supports cards up to 256GB.

Drones:dji-avata-2.explanation: The Avata 2 has 46GB of internal storage and a microSD slot. A U3/V30 card up to 512GB covers its 4K/60 HDR and 10-bit D-Log M modes.

Drones:dji-mini-5-pro.explanation: The Mini 5 Pro records 4K/120 at up to 150 Mbps. DJI requires a U3/V30 card, and a 512GB card holds about 7.5 hours at the top bitrate on top of 42GB of internal storage.

Gaming Handhelds:nintendo-switch.explanation: The Switch reads microSD at UHS-I speed, about 100 MB/s, so any name-brand U1 or U3 card loads games as fast as the console allows. Buy for capacity: 256GB or 512GB holds most digital libraries.

Gaming Handhelds:nintendo-switch-oled.explanation: The Switch OLED has 64GB of internal storage and the same UHS-I microSD slot as the original Switch. A 512GB or 1TB card covers a large digital library.

Gaming Handhelds:steam-deck.explanation: SteamOS runs from the internal SSD, and the microSD slot holds your game library. Buy for capacity first, then pick an A2 card for faster game loads.

Gaming Handhelds:asus-rog-ally.explanation: The original ROG Ally has a UHS-II microSD reader, so a UHS-II card loads games faster than a UHS-I card. Early units had a reader that overheated cards; keep the BIOS and firmware updated.

Gaming Handhelds:nintendo-switch-lite.explanation: The Switch Lite has 32GB of internal storage and a UHS-I microSD slot. A 128GB or 256GB card from a known brand holds a typical library.

Gaming Handhelds:nintendo-switch-2.explanation: The Switch 2 only stores games on microSD Express cards. Your old Switch microSD card can't hold Switch 2 game data; it can only be used once to import screenshots and videos.

Gaming Handhelds:nintendo-3ds-xl.explanation: Nintendo supports SDHC cards up to 32GB in the 3DS family, but 64GB and 128GB cards work once formatted FAT32. The original 3DS and 3DS XL take full-size SD; the New 3DS and New 3DS XL take microSD.

Gaming Handhelds:anbernic-rg353v.explanation: The RG353V has two microSD slots. Put the OS on a 32GB to 64GB A1 or A2 card in TF1 and your ROMs on a 256GB to 512GB card in TF2.

Gaming Handhelds:asus-rog-ally-x.explanation: The ROG Ally X has a UHS-II microSD reader, so a UHS-II card loads games faster than UHS-I. Windows runs from the internal SSD, and the card holds your game library.

Gaming Handhelds:lenovo-legion-go.explanation: The Legion Go runs Windows 11, and AAA games often need 100GB or more each, so capacity is the first decision. Its UHS-I slot caps reads near 100 MB/s, and an A2 card handles the small random reads games make while loading.

Gaming Handhelds:miyoo-mini-plus.explanation: The Miyoo Mini Plus runs its OS and games from one microSD card, so a name-brand A1 card keeps menus responsive. 64GB to 128GB holds thousands of retro games.

Gaming Handhelds:anbernic-rg35xx-plus-h.explanation: The RG35XX Plus and H have two microSD slots. Put the system on a 16 to 32GB A1 card in slot 1 and your ROMs on a larger card in slot 2. Replace the bundled cards first: they are the most common cause of boot failures.

Gaming Handhelds:retroid-pocket-4-pro.explanation: The Retroid Pocket 4 Pro takes a single microSD card for ROMs and Android storage. A 256GB A1 or A2 card holds a large PS1, Dreamcast and GameCube library.

Gaming Handhelds:lenovo-legion-go-s.explanation: The Legion Go S has a UHS-I microSD reader capped near 100 MB/s. A U3/V30 card with an A2 rating runs games well, and UHS-II cards load no faster.

Gaming Handhelds:msi-claw.explanation: The MSI Claw A1M has a UHS-I microSD slot. Buy an A2 card in 512GB or 1TB; UHS-II cards run at UHS-I speed here.

Gaming Handhelds:gpd-win-mini.explanation: The GPD Win Mini runs Windows games from its microSD slot. An A2 V30 card from a known brand, in 512GB or 1TB, holds a PC game library.

Gaming Handhelds:egret-ii-mini.explanation: The Egret II Mini uses its card slot for firmware updates and extra games. Any 32GB or 64GB Class 10 card from a known brand works.

Gaming Handhelds:analogue-pocket.explanation: The Analogue Pocket loads games into FPGA memory before playing, so card speed doesn't affect gameplay. A 64GB to 128GB name-brand card formatted exFAT holds cores and ROMs.

Gaming Handhelds:sony-ps-vita-sd2vita.explanation: A PS Vita only reads microSD through an SD2Vita adapter and custom firmware. 128GB or 256GB cards run smoothly; larger libraries slow the LiveArea home screen.

Gaming Handhelds:anbernic-rg556.explanation: The RG556 has one microSD slot for ROMs alongside its internal storage. A 256GB or 512GB A1 card holds a PS2 and GameCube library.

Gaming Handhelds:r36s.explanation: The R36S ships with unbranded cards that fail often. Replace the OS card (TF1) with a 16GB to 32GB SanDisk card and put ROMs on a 128GB card in TF2. Save the .dtb files from the stock card first.

Gaming Handhelds:retroid-pocket-6.explanation: The Retroid Pocket 6 runs a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 and emulates PS2, GameCube and many Switch games. Switch games take 5GB to 20GB each, so buy a 512GB or 1TB A2 card.

Gaming Handhelds:retroid-pocket-5.explanation: The Retroid Pocket 5 runs PS2 and GameCube games at 2x to 3x resolution. A 512GB A2 card holds a large library of those 1GB to 8GB disc images.

Gaming Handhelds:retroid-pocket-mini.explanation: The Retroid Pocket Mini runs a Snapdragon 865 with a compact AMOLED screen. A 256GB A2 card holds a large PS1, Dreamcast and retro library.

Security Cameras:wyze-cam-v3.explanation: Using a High Endurance microSD card like the SanDisk Extreme PRO 256GB, you can record non-stop videos all day long without worrying about card errors or corrupted footage. This means you'll capture every moment, every movement, and every detail without interruptions. With reliable recording, you can focus on what really matters - keeping your home and loved ones safe and secure.

Security Cameras:eufy-solocam-s340.explanation: Using a Class 10 microSD card with the SoloCam S340 guarantees uninterrupted monitoring, so you can rest assured your footage is consistently recorded and available for review. This ensures you never miss a thing, whether it's an incident or a moment you'll cherish forever. With a reliable microSD card, you can trust that your security footage is safely stored.

Security Cameras:reolink-e1-pro.explanation: With our recommended microSD card, you get crystal-clear video recording without interruptions, allowing you to trust that every crucial moment is captured. Smooth performance means fewer worries about storage errors or footage loss. This setup keeps your security camera system up and running, giving you peace of mind 24/7.

Smartphones:iphone-15.explanation: Enjoy seamless photo and video transfer with your iPhone 15. This means no lengthy waits or frustrating drops in your creative workflow. With external SD card access via USB-C reader, your content is always at your fingertips.

Smartphones:iphone-14.explanation: With a Lightning reader, you can instantly access and transfer your photos and videos without needing to physically plug in your iPhone. This makes sharing and editing your content on the go so much easier. By upgrading to a Lightning reader, you'll have more freedom to capture and share life's moments without interruptions.

Smartphones:iphone-13.explanation: Upgrade to the latest microSD reader and enjoy seamless content transfer between your iPhone 13 and compatible external storage. This keeps your phone clutter-free, letting you focus on capturing more moments, not deleting memories. By expanding your storage, you can keep creating and sharing without interruptions.

Smartphones:iphone-14-pro-max.explanation: With external SD card access via Lightning reader, you can expand your iPhone 14 Pro Max storage seamlessly. This means you'll never have to worry about running out of space for your photos, videos, or files, giving you peace of mind to capture life's moments. Now you'll be able to store, transfer, and manage your media on the go.

Smartphones:iphone-se.explanation: With an external SD card via Lightning reader, you can expand your iPhone SE's storage on the go, freeing up space for more photos, videos, or music without sacrificing performance. This means you can keep taking and playing your favorite content without worrying about running out of room. Enjoy a seamless experience, always.

Smartphones:samsung-galaxy-s23.explanation: With a USB-C reader, you can store and transfer more photos and videos on your Galaxy S23, keeping them organized and easily accessible on the go. This means you can keep your favorite memories and moments just a tap away.

Smartphones:google-pixel-8.explanation: Enabling expanded storage on your Google Pixel 8 or 8 Pro with a USB-C external card reader lets you store more photos, videos, and apps without running out of space. This means you can capture more memories, download more games, and save more files without worrying about running low. With more storage at your fingertips, you can do more on the go.

Drones:potensic-atom-2.explanation: The Atom 2 records 4K/30 HDR from a 1/2-inch sensor and takes U3/V30 microSD cards up to 256GB. A 128GB card covers a full day of flying.

Drones:dji-avata-360.explanation: The Avata 360 records 8K/60 360° video at up to 180 Mbps, about 22.5 MB/s. A U3/V30 microSD card covers that, and 42GB of internal storage holds about 30 minutes of 8K.

Drones:dji-neo.explanation: The DJI Neo has no microSD card slot. It records to 22GB of internal storage, which you empty to your phone with QuickTransfer or to a computer over USB-C.

Drones:dji-mavic-4-pro.explanation: The Mavic 4 Pro records H.264 and H.265 to a UHS-I microSD slot that takes U3/V30 cards up to 1TB. ProRes is only on the 512GB Creator Combo and records to its internal SSD, never the card.

Action Cameras:insta360-x5.explanation: The Insta360 X5 records 8K/30 360 video and needs a V30 UHS-I microSD card, formatted exFAT, up to 1TB.

Action Cameras:dji-osmo-action-6.explanation: The Osmo Action 6 has 64GB of built-in storage and a microSD slot for U3/V30 cards up to 1TB.

Action Cameras:dji-osmo-pocket-4.explanation: The Osmo Pocket 4 has 107GB of built-in storage and a microSD slot that takes U3/V30 cards up to 1TB.

Action Cameras:insta360-ace-pro-2.explanation: The Insta360 Ace Pro 2 records 8K/30 and 4K/120 and needs a V30 UHS-I microSD card.

Action Cameras:gopro-hero-9-black.explanation: The Hero 9 Black records 5K/30 and 4K/60 at up to 100 Mbps. GoPro requires a V30 microSD card and validated capacities up to 256GB.

Drones:dji-lito-x1.explanation: The DJI Lito X1 is a sub-250g drone with 42GB of built-in storage and a microSD slot that takes cards up to 2TB. It records 4K/60 HDR at up to 150 Mbps, so a U3/V30 card covers it.

Gaming Handhelds:rog-xbox-ally-x.explanation: The ROG Xbox Ally X has a UHS-II microSD reader, so UHS-II cards load games faster than UHS-I cards. Buy 1TB or 2TB for a Windows game library.

Gaming Handhelds:lenovo-legion-go-gen-2.explanation: The Legion Go 2 has a UHS-II microSD reader, so UHS-II cards load games faster than UHS-I. Buy 1TB or 2TB: AAA games often exceed 100GB each.

Gaming Handhelds:msi-claw-8-ex-ai-plus.explanation: The MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ has a microSD Express reader rated over 800 MB/s. An Express card loads games far faster than UHS-I, and standard A2 microSD cards still work at UHS-I speed.

Gaming Handhelds:onexplayer-3.explanation: The OneXPlayer 3 runs Windows on Intel's Arc G3 Extreme and has a microSD slot plus a Mini SSD slot. Put your largest games on the SSD and use a 1TB A2 microSD card for the rest.

Gaming Handhelds:anbernic-rg35xx-sp.explanation: The RG35XX SP has two microSD slots: a 16GB to 32GB card in TF1 for the OS and a 128GB to 256GB card in TF2 for ROMs. Replace the bundled cards before you add games.

Gaming Handhelds:anbernic-rg406v-rg406h.explanation: The RG406H and RG406V have 128GB of internal storage and a microSD slot up to 2TB. A 256GB or 512GB A2 card holds a PS2 and GameCube library.

Gaming Handhelds:trimui-brick.explanation: The TrimUI Brick boots its OS from the same microSD card that holds your games, so buy a name-brand A1 card. 64GB to 128GB is plenty for retro games.

Gaming Handhelds:ayn-odin-3-odin-2-porta.explanation: The Odin 3 and Odin 2 Portal emulate PS2, GameCube and Switch games, which take gigabytes each. A 512GB or 1TB A2 card holds a large library.

Gaming Handhelds:anbernic-rg-cube.explanation: The RG Cube's square 3.95-inch screen suits DS, 3DS and classic retro games, which are small files. A 128GB name-brand card is enough for most owners.

Gaming Handhelds:acer-predator-atlas-8.explanation: The Acer Predator Atlas 8 has a UHS-II microSD reader, so UHS-II cards load Windows games faster than UHS-I. Buy 512GB or 1TB for a PC library.

Gaming Handhelds:retroid-pocket-g2.explanation: The Retroid Pocket G2 runs Android 15 on a Snapdragon G2 Gen 2 with 128GB built in. A 512GB A2 card adds room for PS2 and GameCube libraries.

Gaming Handhelds:ayaneo-pocket-ds.explanation: The AYANEO Pocket DS is a dual-screen Android handheld with a Snapdragon G3x Gen 2 and a microSD slot. DS and 3DS games are small, so a 128GB to 256GB name-brand card is enough.

Gaming Handhelds:ayn-thor.explanation: The AYN Thor is a dual-screen Android handheld with a Snapdragon 865 or 8 Gen 2 and a microSD slot. For PS2, GameCube and Switch emulation, buy a 512GB or 1TB A2 card.

Cameras:sony-a1-ii.explanation: Both a1 II slots take CFexpress Type A or SD UHS-II. Use CFexpress Type A for 8K and 30 fps RAW bursts, and V90 SD cards for 4K.

Cameras:canon-eos-r5-mark-ii.explanation: The R5 Mark II has one CFexpress Type B slot and one SD UHS-II slot. 8K RAW and 4K/120 need CFexpress; a V90 SD card works for lower-bitrate modes and backup.

Cameras:canon-powershot-elph-100-hs.explanation: The ELPH 100 HS records 1080p/24 and takes SD, SDHC and SDXC cards. Any Class 4 or faster card works.

Cameras:sony-cybershot-dsc-w800.explanation: The W800 records 720p video and takes SD cards or Memory Stick PRO Duo. Any Class 4 or faster SD card works.

Cameras:nikon-coolpix-s3100.explanation: The Coolpix S3100 records 720p video. Nikon recommends Class 6 or faster SD cards for movies.
